4. Why Saying No Feels So Guilty (People-Pleasing Psychology)

## Description
Why do you say "yes" when every part of you wants to say no?

You're tired. You have your own problems. But before you can even think, your mouth says "Of course." This video explores why people-pleasing can feel like relief, how the fear of rejection, conflict and disapproval can train the mind to agree on autopilot, and what changes when you learn to pause, feel the discomfort, and set a boundary — without becoming cold or unkind.

This is one possible pattern, not a diagnosis. People-pleasing doesn't have one single cause.

4:36 You don't have to abandon yourself to be loved

🧠 KEY IDEAS
• Relief after saying yes can reinforce people-pleasing
• Other people's reactions aren't something you control
• Guilt is a feeling, not always proof you did something wrong
• Discomfort does not automatically mean danger
• You can care about people without abandoning your own needs

If this made you feel seen, subscribe to Zihni Oyunu for more psychology told through minimalist animation, and share it with someone who struggles to say no.

This video is for education and reflection and is not a substitute for professional mental health advice. If people-pleasing is causing you real distress, consider talking to a licensed therapist.
